lessons.title: Lesson 1: LLMs vs Agents

video.title: What are AI Agents?
video.purpose: Understand the difference between a model that answers and an agent that can use tools.

lessons.goal: Reagan can explain the difference between Claude as an LLM and Hermes as an agent in normal words.
sections: Write this in your own words: what is the difference between an AI that answers and an AI that acts?

An LLM is the brain. It predicts, reasons, writes, summarizes, and explains. Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini are LLMs. An agent uses an LLM plus tools, memory, rules, and a goal. The simple line: an LLM thinks and answers. An agent thinks and acts.
Watch the IBM agent video. Write down the first moment where the video moves from talking to doing.
Make a two column chart. Left side: LLM. Right side: agent. Add 5 examples to each side from CJ's world.
Submit your chart and a 4 sentence explanation of why CJ uses agents instead of only chatbots.

quiz.q: What is the cleanest difference between an LLM and an agent?
choices: An LLM answers, an agent can act with tools
They are the exact same thing

quiz.q: Which example fits an agent best?
choices: Explain what a press release is
Search Drive, find a file, update a project, and report proof

lessons.checkpoint: I can explain LLM vs agent without hype.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Claude Setup and First Prompt

video.title: Getting started with Claude.ai
video.purpose: Set up Claude, log in, and understand the first clicks without sitting through a long video.

lessons.goal: Reagan creates or logs into Claude and runs a useful first prompt.
sections: Claude is where you go when you need a smart thinking partner. It is strong for writing, planning, summarizing, and explaining.
Go to claude.ai. Create or log into your account. Confirm you can start a new chat. Do not add private passwords, tokens, or client info.
Watch the 5:19 Anthropic video. Pause after the first prompt example and write what made the prompt clear.
Ask Claude to create a 5 step plan for setting up your AI workspace for this course. Then ask it to make the plan shorter and more direct.
Submit a screenshot showing Claude open and paste the final 5 step plan into your workbook.

quiz.q: What is Claude best used for in this course?
What should you avoid pasting into Claude?
What makes a first prompt useful?
choices: Context, goal, constraints, and desired output

lessons.checkpoint: I have Claude open and know how to start clean.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Codex Setup and When to Use It

video.title: Using OpenAI Codex CLI with GPT-5-Codex
video.purpose: See Codex from the official OpenAI channel and understand how it differs from Claude.

lessons.goal: Reagan creates or logs into Codex and understands when Codex is the right tool.
sections: Codex is for building, editing, reviewing, and checking work. Think of it as another smart teammate, not a magic button.
Create or log into the account CJ provides. Confirm you can open Codex and start a task. Keep private data out of test prompts.
Watch the OpenAI video. Write one thing Codex does that feels different from a normal chat.
Give Codex a simple sample task: review this checklist for clarity. Use fake content, not private CJ business data.
Submit a screenshot showing Codex access and 3 bullets on when you would choose Codex instead of Claude.

choices: For building, editing, reviewing, or checking work

lessons.checkpoint: I can open Codex and know what job it should do.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Set Up Your Hermes Agent in Telegram
lessons.goal: Reagan gets her Hermes agent working in Telegram and knows the first commands to use.
sections: Hermes is the agent system. Telegram is the front door. You message the agent like a person, but it can use tools behind the scenes.
Install Telegram, create or log into your account, and connect with the Hermes bot CJ provides. If CJ gives a pairing or approval step, complete it with him watching.
Test /help, /new, /model, /tools, and /skills. Write one sentence explaining what each command does.
Send Hermes a safe practice task: explain what tools you have access to and what you cannot do yet. Do not ask it to edit anything real.
Submit a screenshot of your Telegram agent responding and your 5 command notes.

quiz.q: What is Telegram in this setup?
choices: The front door to the agent

quiz.q: What should Reagan do before asking Hermes to change real files?
choices: Understand the task and proof needed

lessons.checkpoint: I have my Hermes agent reachable in Telegram.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Markdown and MD Files
lessons.goal: Reagan understands why agents use Markdown and can write a simple MD instruction file.
sections: Markdown is plain text with structure. Agents read it well because it is clear, portable, and easy to edit.
Headings create sections. Bullets create lists. Checkboxes create action steps. Code blocks preserve exact commands or examples.
Create a file called my-ai-workspace.md. Add headings for Accounts, Agent Commands, Rules, and Proof.
Write a short instruction block for your agent: what you want help with, what it should never do, and what proof you expect.

quiz.q: Why do agents like MD files?
choices: They are clear and easy to parse

quiz.q: What belongs in an agent instruction file?
choices: Goals, rules, context, and proof requirements

lessons.checkpoint: I can write a simple MD file an agent can follow.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Skills, Commands, Tools, and MCPs
lessons.goal: Reagan knows the difference between the agent building blocks CJ talks about.
sections: These words sound technical at first. They are not that complicated. They are how an agent knows what to do and what it can touch.
Skills are saved playbooks. Commands are shortcuts. Tools are actions the agent can take. MCPs are connections to outside systems. Memory is durable context that should still matter later.
Skill: how to update Mission Control. Command: /new. Tool: read a file. MCP: connect to an app or data source.
Make a glossary with one definition and one example for MD, skill, command, tool, API, MCP, memory, and agent.
Submit the glossary and one question you still have.

choices: A connection that lets an agent use outside tools or data

lessons.checkpoint: I can explain the agent building blocks without mixing them up.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: First Project, My AI Workspace
lessons.goal: Reagan finishes Week 1 with Claude, Codex, and Hermes working and a clean setup guide she can use again.
sections: Your first project is not fake. Set up your own AI workspace. By the end, you should have Claude, Codex, Telegram, and Hermes ready to use.
Include screenshots or notes proving Claude login, Codex login, Telegram setup, Hermes response, and your glossary.
Create My AI Workspace setup guide. Include accounts, links, first prompts, commands tested, glossary, rules, and what to ask CJ for if something is blocked.
Ask Claude to make the guide clearer. Ask Codex to check for missing steps. Ask Hermes what proof CJ would want before marking it complete.
Submit the guide, proof screenshots, quiz score, and a 2 minute walkthrough for CJ.

quiz.q: What accounts should be working by the end?

choices: Working access, setup guide, glossary, and proof

lessons.checkpoint: I have my AI workspace set up and can prove it.
